text:
maria: quick question about async job cancellation semantics — we're adding an abort flow for the long-running transform endpoint. need to pick a contract that is easy for clients and safe for backcompat. thoughts?

raj: current behavior for /v1/transform is: POST -> 202 + {operation_id} and clients poll GET /operations/:id. cancel today is POST /operations/:id:cancel which returns 200 + {status: \"cancelling\"}. sometimes racey though.

oliver: i'd push to make cancel idempotent and return the updated operation object (like the GET) with a `terminal: boolean` and `status` enum. that way client doesn't need an extra GET after cancel. example:

```
POST /operations/abcd:cancel
200
{
  "id": "abcd",
  "status": "cancelled",
  "terminal": true,
  "updated_at": "2025-11-12T10:02:03Z"
}
```

natalie: +1 on idempotency, but what about the HTTP code? returning 200 vs 202 matters for some SDKs. 202 signals "work in progress". If cancel request triggers async work (signal to worker) maybe it should be 202 and include operation state.

raj: we need to be careful with existing clients that parse for 200 meaning success+result. historically they expected 200 to mean operation finished (bad). we documented 200 for GET only. not many clients hit :cancel but still.

maria: options:
- keep current POST :cancel -> 200 with operation object (but change semantics to allow non-terminal status like \"cancelling\")
- switch to 202 + operation object to show it's accepted (and still include current status)
- add `prefer: respond-async` style header? maybe too fancy.

oliver: implementation wise, workers acknowledge cancel asynchronously; so 202 feels more accurate. but returning the op object in the body (with status maybe \"cancelling\") is helpful.

natalie: compatibility proposal: default to 202. add `X-Compat-Return: immediate` header clients can set to get 200+terminal if they really want synchronous behavior (but default remains safe). we add a note to changelog and mark as non-breaking because body shape remains same.

raj: small nit — normalize the status enum values: proposed set {\"queued\", \"running\", \"cancelling\", \"cancelled\", \"failed\", \"succeeded\"}. add `terminal` = status in {cancelled, failed, succeeded}.

maria: agreed. also want a `client_request_id` echo back if provided in initial POST to help de-dup and tracing. Request id is required for idempotency docs.

oliver: for polling semantics, clients will often poll `GET /operations/:id` which returns 200 + op. make sure `retry-after` header is set when server thinks polling should backoff for throttling/batching.

natalie: security/observability note: when a cancel is requested we need to emit audit event with who requested it and attach the `reason` field if provided. suggest `POST /operations/:id:cancel {"reason":"string"}`.

maria: draft response contract for cancel (compatible body shape):
```
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "id": "abcd",
  "status": "cancelling",
  "terminal": false,
  "updated_at": "2025-11-12T10:02:03Z",
  "request_id": "req_123",
  "client_request_id": "orig-client-789"
}
```

raj: tests to add:
- cancel is idempotent (repeat POST returns same or consistent state)
- header `Retry-After` present for heavy load cases
- operation transitions eventually to terminal state

deploy-bot: CI: cancel-contract-tests failing on staging — see job 8342 (https://ci.internal/jobs/8342) :eyes:

maria: @raj can you pick up the failing test? i'll update the API docs and compatibility note. also will add example SDK code for Node + Python.

raj: on it, filing a tiny PR to make 202 default and include op body: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/422 — will add changelog entry.

oliver: sdk ergonomics: for convenience we should expose a helper `operation.cancel({wait:false})` which calls the :cancel endpoint and optionally polls until terminal. would reduce client boilerplate.

natalie: sounds good. one last ask: ensure telemetry emits a metric when cancels are frequent for a given model — could indicate upstream infra issues.

maria: perfect. i'll push the spec draft + samples to the docs repo after raj's PR merges. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
